decisions.summary: the rolled place's slide stops when the seat's OUTER edge would pass the gable (abs(nx) + w/2 > half_wall)
decisions.why: Round 1's NOT LEGITIMATE answered: along_its_wall now yields only seats wholly along the wall, matching 0047's 'under the eaves by the stable', the plan's 'only while the WHOLE seat stands along its wall' and the page's 'while the whole privy still stands along the wall'. test_a_slide_along_the_wall_stops_at_the_walls_end asserts containment for every yielded seat. Nothing is excepted any more, so it is a within decision. Not blocking: test_a_rolled_stable_privy_never_stands_past_the_walls_end still asserts the INNER edge (abs(x) - w/2 <= HW/2), which is weaker than its own name.

decisions.summary: row 564 held, re-tiered E2 -> E3 on a per-household measure: 16 of 16 households that rolled the stable or the front are refused it, the yard covering the rolled spot on all 16 and no slide step fitting wholly along the wall on any
decisions.why: Round 1 asked for exactly this measure, per rolled household and per offered seat. It now shows the yard blocking the rolled spot on every one, and the wall-end bound leaving no slide step, because the spots already stand near the wall's end. That bound is the research's own 'under the eaves'. So no seat order honors the roll, and the remaining fix is a layout change to the yard: real work above E2. Holding it and re-tiering it applies the GM's own ranking ('easiest to hardest'), with the row kept open rather than dropped. The override states the count, and its files now name bundle.py and yards.py.
